Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int Items(IntPtr self, uint flags, ref Guid iid, out IntPtr result)
Rationale: IFolderView::Items is vtable slot 8 (IUnknown 0-2, GetCurrentViewMode 3 .. ItemCount 7, Items 8 counted from the documented method order); ItemsDelegate(self, uint flags, ref Guid iid, out IntPtr) matches (SVGIO flags, REFIID, void**); HRESULT returned as int, no PreserveSig loss. The only caller checks hr<0 and zero pointer. No direct test (ExplorerNativeVtable has none); exercised only by the real-shell ExplorerOrderServiceTests.ProgressiveSnapshotRunsSafely.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int EnumNext(IntPtr self, uint count, IntPtr[] items, out uint fetched)
Rationale: IEnumIDList::Next is slot 3 and EnumNextDelegate takes [Out] IntPtr[] (blittable, pinned) plus out uint fetched, as Next(ULONG, PITEMID_CHILD*, ULONG*) requires. The wrapper does not bound count against items.Length, but its single caller passes children.Length. No direct test.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int QueryService(IntPtr self, ref Guid service, ref Guid iid, out IntPtr result)
Rationale: IServiceProvider::QueryService is slot 3 with (REFGUID, REFIID, void**); delegate uses ref Guid for both GUIDs and out IntPtr, so no marshalling copy issue. Caller releases browserPtr in its finally. No direct test.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int QueryActiveShellView(IntPtr self, out IntPtr view)
Rationale: IShellBrowser::QueryActiveShellView = slot 15 (IOleWindow 3-4, InsertMenusSB 5 ... SendControlMsg 14, QueryActiveShellView 15); out IntPtr is an AddRef'ed IShellView released by the caller's finally. No direct test.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int ItemCount(IntPtr self, uint flags, out int count)
Rationale: IFolderView::ItemCount is slot 7 (flags uint, out int); the caller treats hr<0 or count<=0 as NativeViewUnavailable(EmptyView), so an empty folder or a failing call never reaches the enumeration. No direct test.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int GetGroupBy(IntPtr self, out PROPERTYKEY key, out bool ascending)
Rationale: IFolderView2::GetGroupBy slot 18 (IFolderView ends at 16, SetGroupBy 17); PROPERTYKEY out plus BOOL marshalled as 4-byte Bool. A failing HRESULT is mapped to 'not grouped' by the caller, see P-EXP-01 on TryReadNativeView (the wrapper itself is correct).

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int GetSortColumnCount(IntPtr self, out int count)
Rationale: IFolderView2::GetSortColumnCount slot 26 (GetCurrentFolderFlags 25 then 26); out int. ReadSortColumns bounds the result to 1..32 before allocating, so a bogus count cannot drive a huge array.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.internal static int GetSortColumns(IntPtr self, SORTCOLUMN[] columns, int count)
Rationale: IFolderView2::GetSortColumns slot 28 (SetSortColumns 27); SORTCOLUMN {PROPERTYKEY{Guid,uint}, int} is blittable sequential, so [Out] array pinning is safe; caller passes native.Length as count so no overrun. No direct test.

IFolderView2::GetItem slot 29 resolved once per view; delegate (self, int index, ref Guid iid, out IntPtr) matches GetItem(int, REFIID, void**). Returned delegate is reused only against folderViewPtr (same vtable) as the per-item loop does.

IShellItem::GetDisplayName slot 5 (BindToHandler 3, GetParent 4); delegate (self, uint sigdn, out IntPtr name). Per-item loop caches the delegate per distinct vtable address, so a heterogeneous item implementation cannot receive a delegate bound to another vtable.

Function: ExplorerNativeVtable.private static T Get<T>(IntPtr self, int slot) where T : Delegate
Rationale: Generic slot reader: ReadIntPtr(self) then ReadIntPtr(vtable, slot*IntPtr.Size) then GetDelegateForFunctionPointer<T>. Correct pointer arithmetic for x64. A null self would AV, but every caller guards IntPtr.Zero first. Allocates a new delegate per call (perf only, per-item path resolves once per vtable).

Constructor assigns _log before Thread.Start so RunLoop can log; thread is STA, IsBackground=true and named. SetApartmentState before Start is the only legal order. Covered by ExplorerOrderServiceSeamTests.QueriesAreSerializedOnOneStaThread.

GetConsumingEnumerable loop drains remaining queued actions after CompleteAdding; per-action try/catch logs and keeps the pump alive (action wrappers already catch, this is a backstop). Covered by QueryThatThrowsIsReportedAsFailedAndThePumpSurvives.

Enqueue uses RunContinuationsAsynchronously so awaiting callers never run on the STA thread; _queue.Add after CompleteAdding/Dispose throws InvalidOperationException (ObjectDisposedException derives from it) and is converted to a faulted ObjectDisposedException task, which TryGetSnapshotCoreAsync catches. Test: DisposeIsIdempotentAndLaterUseIsCancelledNotThrown.

Work wrapper uses TrySetResult/TrySetException so a late completion after the caller gave up cannot throw; exceptions from work() are routed into the task, not the pump thread. Covered by the seam tests above.

Interlocked guard makes Dispose idempotent (singleton disposed by window and DI container). 200 ms Join then leak-on-stuck-COM is documented (R2-F-30) and logged; queue only disposed after the thread exited so a late Add cannot hit a disposed collection unobserved. Test: DisposeCancelsPrefetchAndDoesNotHangOnAStuckQuery.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.public ExplorerOrderService(ILog? log = null) : this(log, null)
Rationale: Public ctor forwards to the internal one with query=null so the real QueryShell is used; no logic of its own.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.internal ExplorerOrderService(ILog? log, ExplorerQuery? query, TimeProvider? time = null, TimeSpan? prefetchMaxAge = null)
Rationale: Seams default sensibly (QueryShell, TimeProvider.System, DefaultPrefetchMaxAge); _pump is created last so a throwing argument cannot leave a started thread. The thread starts in the ctor and is only stopped by Dispose, which MainWindow/DI both call (AR02c).

Sets _disposed first, takes and cancels the stored prefetch (Cancel tolerates an already-disposed CTS), then disposes the pump; the late-store race in Prefetch is closed by the locked _disposed re-check. Test: PrefetchRacingDispose_StoresNothing.

Cancel swallows ObjectDisposedException because the cleanup continuation disposes Cts when the query ends (RV-P04); no other exception is possible from CTS.Cancel with a non-throwing callback set. Test: FinishedPrefetch_ReleasesTokenSource_AndLaterCancelIsSafe.
Test seam read under _prefetchGate, consistent with every other access of _prefetch.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private static bool TryCanonicalize(string? folder, out string canonical)
Rationale: Rejects null/whitespace and maps ArgumentException/NotSupportedException/PathTooLongException from GetFullPath (embedded NUL, bad colon) to false so callers report Failed instead of throwing. Test: InvalidFolderIsReportedNotThrown.
Builds a Failed snapshot with the ArgumentException name as reason; folder?? string.Empty covers null input, so no NRE.
Atomic take-and-clear under the lock gives the one-shot join semantics; no await inside the lock.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.public void Prefetch(string folder, TimeSpan timeout)
Rationale: Order is correct: query started, cleanup continuation attached, then the locked store re-checks _disposed; superseded prefetch cancelled outside the lock; unstored one cancelled. Prefetch passes progress=null and batch 16, which the sole caller does as well. Tests: NewPrefetchSupersedesAndCancelsThePreviousOne, PrefetchRacingDispose_StoresNothing.
Static lambda disposes the CTS passed as state, ExecuteSynchronously on the default scheduler; no capture, so no leak of this. Covered by FinishedPrefetch_ReleasesTokenSource_AndLaterCancelIsSafe.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.public Task<ExplorerViewSnapshot> TryGetSnapshotProgressiveAsync(string folder, TimeSpan timeout, IProgress<ExplorerQueryProgress>? progress = null, int batchSize = 16, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: batchSize clamped 1..128; a stored prefetch for another folder or older than 30 s is cancelled so it stops occupying the single STA thread, a fresh same-folder one is joined (SamePath compares canonical spellings). The progress argument is dropped when joining, but FolderLoadCoordinator.cs:99-104 passes null, so no observable loss. Tests: PrefetchIsJoinedOnceRegardlessOfPathSpelling, StalePrefetchIsNotJoined, FreshPrefetchIsJoined.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private static async Task<ExplorerViewSnapshot> JoinPrefetchAsync(PrefetchedQuery prefetched, TimeSpan timeout, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: WaitAsync with NormalizeTimeout and the caller token; timeout and cancellation both cancel the shared prefetch and return Timed Out / Canceled snapshots instead of throwing. A prefetch that itself faulted cannot happen (core catches). Tests: JoinedPrefetchHonoursCallerTimeout, JoinedPrefetchHonoursCallerCancellation.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.public async Task<ExplorerViewSnapshot> TryGetSnapshotAsync(string folder, TimeSpan timeout, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: Thin wrapper over the core with batchSize=int.MaxValue (disables the Thread.Yield cadence); never consumes the prefetch slot, which is intentional.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private async Task<ExplorerViewSnapshot> TryGetSnapshotCoreAsync(string folder, TimeSpan timeout, IProgress<ExplorerQueryProgress>? progress, int batchSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: Linked CTS with CancelAfter(NormalizeTimeout) bounds the caller's wait while the work cancels itself at COM-call boundaries; Canceled-vs-TimedOut decided by whether the caller token fired; ObjectDisposedException from a shut pump is mapped to Canceled; timeoutCts disposal after return is safe (token stays valid). A hung explorer.exe still blocks the single STA queue, but each caller times out (documented design). Tests: TimeoutReleasesCallerCancelsWorkAndFreesPump, CallerCancellationBeatsExpiredTimeout.

Query runs on the STA; OperationCanceledException becomes a Canceled snapshot via ResolveCancellation, any other exception is logged and becomes Failed with only the exception type name in the reason (no path/HRESULT text leaked). Test: QueryThatThrowsIsReportedAsFailedAndThePumpSurvives.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.internal static ExplorerViewSnapshot ResolveCancellation(ExplorerViewSnapshot snapshot, bool disposed, CancellationToken callerToken, CancellationToken linkedToken)
Rationale: Pure decision: caller cancellation and disposal win, otherwise linked token fired means TimedOut; non-Canceled results untouched. Tests: ResolveCancellationPicksTheRightStatus, ResolveCancellationKeepsOtherStatuses.

Infinite kept, negative becomes zero, and values above uint.MaxValue-1 ms become Infinite because CancelAfter/WaitAsync reject larger delays; exactly the documented .NET limit. Test: NegativeTimeoutMeansExpiredNotException.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private ExplorerViewSnapshot QueryShell(string folder, IProgress<ExplorerQueryProgress>? progress, int batchSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: Late-bound Shell.Application.Windows() enumeration: the ((IEnumerable)windows).Cast<object>() enumerator wraps a COM IEnumVARIANT RCW that is not IDisposable, so it is never FinalReleased (windows and shell are). Reclaimed by the GC finalizer only, on a non-STA thread; harmless in practice but inconsistent with the otherwise exact release discipline. See P-COM-01. Null windows result is covered (Cast throws, converted to Failed by the pump lambda). No direct test of the real path.

locationOf lambda reads dynamic LocationURL; a closed window or non-browser entry raises COMException/RuntimeBinderException which ExplorerWindowSelector skips (test WindowClosingDuringLocationReadIsSkipped); a null window item also lands in RuntimeBinderException.

read lambda forwards progress, batchSize and token to TryReadNativeView; every exception is converted by the selector to a Failed snapshot with type and HRESULT, cancellation to Canceled. Test: ThrownReadIsReportedWithTypeAndHresult.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private ExplorerViewSnapshot TryReadNativeView(object window, string folder, IProgress<ExplorerQueryProgress>? progress, int batchSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: COM pointers are balanced (GetIUnknownForObject, QueryInterface x2, QueryService and QueryActiveShellView outputs each released in the finally in reverse order; per-item and PIDL frees correct). Defect is only metadata: 'grouped' is computed as GetGroupBy(...)>=0 && key!=null, so a FAILED GetGroupBy reports ExplorerGroupState.None instead of Unknown, and ReadSortColumns returns [] on failure; both are diagnostic-only today (DiagnosticsWindow shows SortColumns.Count/GroupState) but state a certainty the code does not have. See P-EXP-01. Order data itself is validated downstream by ExplorerSnapshotValidator (set equality with scanned files, InFolder, duplicates), which also neutralises a wrong-tab view on Windows 11.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.private static List<string>? TryReadViewOrderBatched(IntPtr folderView, string folder, int expectedCount, CancellationToken cancellationToken, out string? reason)
Rationale: children array is sized min(expectedCount,512) and zeroed after each Next batch, so the finally FreeChildren cannot double-free or free stale PIDLs; every ILCombine result and SHGetNameFromIDList string is freed on all paths including the early 'return null'; enumPtr released; item count must equal expectedCount or the caller falls back to the per-item loop; S_FALSE or fetched==0 ends the loop. Folder over MAX_PATH makes SHParseDisplayName fail and cleanly falls back. Cancellation checked per batch. No direct test of the native body.
Local function frees each non-zero PIDL with CoTaskMemFree (PIDLs are CoTaskMem allocations) and nulls the slot, which is what makes the per-batch call plus the final-finally call idempotent.

Bounds count to 1..32 before allocating (good) and maps direction 1/-1 to Ascending/Descending (SORT_ASCENDING=1, SORT_DESCENDING=-1, correct), but any failing HRESULT silently returns an empty array, indistinguishable from 'view has no sort columns'. Diagnostic-only; see P-EXP-01.
Pure projection of SORTCOLUMN to ExplorerSortColumn; unknown direction values map to Unknown rather than throwing.

Function: ExplorerOrderService.internal static ExplorerViewSnapshot Unavailable(string folder, ExplorerOrderStatus status, string reason)
Rationale: Factory for unavailable snapshots with empty lists and GroupState.Unknown; no shared mutable collections (fresh [] each call).

Release is FinalReleaseComObject only for real COM objects (IsComObject guard), null-safe; runs on the pump STA thread where the RCWs were created. FinalRelease is safe here because each RCW comes from this query's own enumeration.

Function: ExplorerWindowSelector.internal static ExplorerViewSnapshot Select<TWindow>(string folder, IEnumerable<TWindow> windows, Func<TWindow, string?> locationOf, Func<TWindow, ExplorerViewSnapshot> read, Action<TWindow> release, ILog log, Stopwatch? timer, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
Rationale: Release-exactly-once is guaranteed by the per-window try/finally even on continue/return; MoveNext failure (RV-P03) keeps results found so far; a Canceled snapshot or caller cancellation stops the walk, Available returns at once, other failures are remembered (firstFailure) and the walk continues to the next window on the same folder. Early return leaves un-enumerated windows untouched. Tests: MultipleMatchingWindowsFallThroughFailures, EnumeratorMoveNextFailure_*, CancellationDuringReadStopsTheWalkAndReleases.

Function: ExplorerWindowSelector.internal static bool TryCanonicalizeLocation(string? location, out string folder)
Rationale: Uri.TryCreate absolute + IsFile gate, LocalPath for percent-decoding and UNC (file://srv/share), then CanonicalizeFolder; ArgumentException/NotSupported/PathTooLong mapped to false (shell namespace URLs like file:///::{GUID} fail GetFullPath and are skipped). Tests: TryCanonicalizeLocationDecodesFileUrls, TryCanonicalizeLocationRejectsNonFileLocations, UncLocationMatchesUncFolder.

Function: InstanceScope.public InstanceScope( InstanceMode mode, Action<IReadOnlyList<string>> onForwardedPaths, ILog? log = null, string namePrefix = InstanceKeys.DefaultPrefix, TimeSpan? forwardTimeout = null, bool allowServerForeground = false) : this(mode, onForwardedPaths, log, namePrefix, forwardTimeout, null, allowServerForeground)
Rationale: Public ctor only forwards with clientFactory=null; default factory builds InstanceForwardClient with the scope's own log and allowServerForeground.

Function: InstanceScope.internal InstanceScope( InstanceMode mode, Action<IReadOnlyList<string>> onForwardedPaths, ILog? log, string namePrefix, TimeSpan? forwardTimeout, Func<string, IInstanceForwardClient>? clientFactory, bool allowServerForeground = false)
Rationale: Validates namePrefix (not blank) and onForwardedPaths (not null); the default-client lambda reads _log which is assigned before any call; forwardTimeout defaults to SecondInstanceHandoff.DefaultTimeout and a zero/negative value is not rejected here but SendAsync/TryForwardAsync turn any failure into a normal 'not forwarded' outcome. Undefined InstanceMode values behave as SingleWindow in InstanceKeys.For. Covered by every InstanceScopeTests case.
Factory lambda captures this only to read _log/allowServerForeground and creates a new client per call (no shared state, no handle kept), so there is nothing to dispose.

Function: RecycleBinCapacityGuard.internal static RecycleCapacityVerdict Evaluate(string path, long? fileSize, IRecycleBinSettingsSource source, ILog? log = null)
Rationale: Single fail-closed funnel: the catch-all converts ANY exception (registry type mismatch, long path, Win32 failure) into Unknown and logs only the file name; ArgumentException guards null/blank path and null source. Tests: Evaluate_SourceThrows_Unknown, Evaluate_RealSource_MalformedPath_ReturnsUnknownWithoutThrowing.

Function: RecycleBinCapacityGuard.private static RecycleCapacityVerdict EvaluateCore(string path, long? fileSize, IRecycleBinSettingsSource source)
Rationale: Decision order is sound (policy NoRecycleFiles/legacy nuke, then volume nuke, size-independent Fits when fileSize null, negative size Unknown, percent-policy vs per-volume vs 5 percent default, margin 1 MiB; quota/100*percent cannot overflow). Gap: a volume that resolves via GetVolumePathName but has no BitBucket entry is treated as a default-bin volume whatever its type, so a mounted-folder or junction-reached removable/network volume (no bin) yields Fits (fileSize null) or a 5 percent capacity. Together with CanRecycle's lexical root this is P-RB-01. Existing size/zero-capacity boundaries are well covered by RecycleBinCapacityGuardTests.

Reads NoRecycleFiles from HKCU and HKLM, RecycleBinSize taking the smaller when both exist (conservative), and the legacy HKCU BitBucket NukeOnDelete; a present value that is not a DWORD throws and the guard turns that into Unknown. No dedicated test of the registry reads (guard tests use a fake source).

GetVolumePathName then GetVolumeNameForVolumeMountPoint with a 64-char buffer (volume GUID path is 49 chars + NUL) and ExtractGuid; any failing call returns null which the guard maps to Unknown (subst/network drives therefore refuse, fail closed). Observed on this machine: GetVolumePathNameW follows a junction to D:\ (evidence P-RB-01). Test: RealSource_TempVolume_ResolvesAndSmallFileFits, RealSource_GetVolumeGuid_NonexistentPathOnTempDrive_ResolvesTempDriveGuid.

Builds BitBucket\Volume\{guid} under HKCU and reads NukeOnDelete and MaxCapacity (MB DWORD); absent values stay null; ArgumentException on blank guid. GUID text comes only from ExtractGuid (validated B-format), so no registry path injection.

GetDiskFreeSpaceEx total-bytes output is the quota-aware size for the calling user; zero or above long.MaxValue returns null, which the guard maps to Unknown; no SetLastError use needed because failure is just null.

Prefix match case-insensitive, finds the closing brace, slices {...} and validates with Guid.TryParseExact(\"B\"); index arithmetic (prefix.Length-1 .. close inclusive) checked. Test: ExtractGuid_ParsesVolumeName.

Path.GetFullPath then GetVolumePathNameW into a buffer sized clamp(len+2, 262, 32768) with the correct char[] [Out] marshalling; failure or empty result returns null. A path over the buffer limit throws PathTooLongException from GetFullPath which the guard catches as Unknown. Tests: Evaluate_RealSource_MalformedPath_ReturnsUnknownWithoutThrowing, Evaluate_RealSource_UnmountedDriveLetter_ReturnsUnknown.
Null-safe non-zero test used for the policy switches; trivial and correct (null means off).

Function: WindowsRecycleBinSettingsSource.private static long? ReadDword(RegistryKey hive, string subKey, string name)
Rationale: OpenSubKey(writable:false) with using; absent key or value returns null, REG_DWORD (int) converted with unchecked((uint)) so values above 2^31 are not negative, any other value kind (QWORD, string) throws InvalidDataException which Evaluate converts to Unknown (fail closed).

Zero handle returns false; tries DWMWA 20 then the legacy 19 with the same value and treats any non-S_OK HRESULT as false; DllNotFound/EntryPointNotFound caught. Informational only (callers ignore false). Test: WindowsDarkTitleBarEnablesDarkModeOnARealHandle.

Function: WindowsDarkTitleBar.public static bool TrySetCaptionColor(IntPtr handle, uint colorBgr)
Rationale: Zero handle false; passes the COLORREF (BGR) uint by ref with size 4 to DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR (35, Windows 11 only, E_INVALIDARG elsewhere returns false); missing dwmapi caught. A value with high bits set is rejected by DWM and reported false. No dedicated test.

Function: WindowsDarkTitleBar.private static bool TrySet(IntPtr handle, int attribute, ref int value)
Rationale: Calls the ref-int overload with sizeof(int) and compares HRESULT to 0; the two DllImport overloads share one entry point, which is fine for blittable by-ref args; native exceptions are not expected from DwmSetWindowAttribute.
Only stores the logger (NullLog default); the vblank thread is started lazily by GetTiming, so constructing the static Instance has no side effect.

Correctly records the failed monitor and timestamp and clears _thread under _gate so the next GetTiming can retry after 8 s. But none of its callers (TryOpen failure, D3DKMTWaitForVerticalBlankEvent != 0, DllNotFound/EntryPointNotFound catch) logs anything, so a permanently degraded clock (DWM fallback describes the PRIMARY display only) leaves no diagnostic on a secondary-monitor user's machine. See P-DISP-01.

Zero or invalid window falls back to DwmTiming; monitor lookup uses MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST; _lastUse written before the lock and thread start/failed-monitor retry decided under _gate; published estimate returned only when it belongs to the same monitor, else null (caller falls back). Test: GetTiming_ZeroHandle_ReturnsDwmFallbackTiming; real monitor path only exercised by KineticPanFrameMeasurementTests.

Struct layouts checked field by field against the native ones (OPENADAPTERFROMHDC 24 bytes on x64, WAITFORVERTICALBLANKEVENT 12, MONITORINFOEXW 104) and adapter close happens in finally on every exit; idle exit and monitor-follow logic are consistent under _gate. Suspect: D3DKMTWaitForVerticalBlankEvent can block indefinitely when the monitor is powered off or the session is locked, so the idle check at the loop top is never reached, _thread stays non-null and GetTiming keeps returning the last _published phase until the display wakes. Not proven (no display-sleep run); see P-DISP-02. No test of Run itself.

Function: WindowsDisplayClock.private static bool TryOpen(IntPtr monitor, out uint adapter, out uint source)
Rationale: GetMonitorInfo with Size set, CreateDC on the \\.\DISPLAYn device name, D3DKMTOpenAdapterFromHdc, then DeleteDC in finally on both success and failure; adapter handle only handed out on success, outputs zeroed first so a failure never leaks a stale handle into Close. P/Invoke without SetLastError is fine since only success/failure is used.

Function: WindowsDisplayClock.private static void Close(ref uint adapter)
Rationale: Closes only a non-zero handle and zeroes it, so repeated calls from the follow-monitor path and the final finally are idempotent; status ignored on purpose (nothing to recover).

TimingInfo size read via Marshal.SizeOf (Pack=1 layout of DWM_TIMING_INFO listed in header order, 'only leading fields are read' so a trailing mismatch only changes the size check); non-zero HRESULT, missing dwmapi, or zero QpcRefreshPeriod/QpcVBlank return null; hwnd=0 means primary display, as documented in the class summary. Test: GetTiming_ZeroHandle_ReturnsDwmFallbackTiming.

Function: WindowsLiveOperationRegistry.public WindowsLiveOperationRegistry(ILog? log = null, string prefix = InstanceKeys.DefaultPrefix)
Rationale: Rejects a blank prefix, stores logger default NullLog; no kernel object is created until Begin.

Name is Local\<prefix>_LiveOp_<SHA-256 hex of liveop|SID|id>: fixed length, no illegal kernel-name characters whatever the journal Id holds, per user. A very long prefix could exceed the 260-char object-name limit, which Begin/IsLive convert via ArgumentException handling. Test: NameFor_DistinctPerIdAndPrefix.

Creates a manual-reset event (no thread affinity, so released from any pool thread) and ignores createdNew deliberately, so two holders of one Id share the name until both dispose; failures (IOException, UnauthorizedAccess, name taken by another object type, bad name) log and return the NoMarker singleton, matching the documented 'never fail the file action for its marker' contract (accepted trade-off, Q-R27 / ILiveOperationRegistry). Tests: Begin_SameIdTwice_LiveUntilLastHolderReleases, Begin_NameTakenByMutex_ReturnsNoMarkerAndLogs, Begin_OddIds_SanitisedAndWork.

TryOpenExisting then immediate Dispose of the probe handle (no leak); UnauthorizedAccessException is treated as live (an elevated owner's event), other IO/argument failures log and answer not-live, which equals pre-Q-R27 reconcile behaviour and is the accepted degradation per ILiveOperationRegistry.cs docs. Test: Begin_VisibleToSecondRegistry_UntilDisposed.
Intentional no-op for the shared NoMarker instance; safe to Dispose any number of times or concurrently.
Stores logger only; the static Instance is allocation-free.

Function: WindowsMemoryProbe.public bool HasHeadroom(double maximumLoad, long reserveBytes)
Rationale: Delegates to the pure rule with the freshly taken snapshot; no caching, so each call costs one GlobalMemoryStatusEx (cheap, no disk). Test: WindowsMemoryProbeReportsRealisticMetrics.

Function: WindowsMemoryProbe.public static bool EvaluateHeadroom(MemorySnapshot? snapshot, double maximumLoad, long reserveBytes)
Rationale: Fail-closed on null snapshot; load strictly below maximumLoad*100 (a NaN maximumLoad compares false = no headroom); negative reserve clamped with Math.Max before the ulong cast (RV-P06 wrap bug closed). Tests: EvaluateHeadroom_NullSnapshot_ReportsNoHeadroom, EvaluateHeadroom_ReserveBoundary, EvaluateHeadroom_NegativeReserve_TreatedAsZero, EvaluateHeadroom_LoadAtOrAboveLimit_ReportsNoHeadroom.

MEMORYSTATUSEX layout checked (4+4+7x8 = 64 bytes, Length set from Marshal.SizeOf); SetLastError=true and GetLastWin32Error read immediately in the failure branch; failure logs and returns null which EvaluateHeadroom turns into no headroom.

Function: WindowsNaturalComparer.public int Compare(string? x, string? y)
Rationale: Reference/null ordering handled before the P/Invoke; StrCmpLogicalW truncates at an embedded NUL so equal-looking results fall back to OrdinalIgnoreCase, which still separates them; only DllNotFound/EntryPointNotFound fall back to the managed comparer (CORE-12). Fuzzed 220 random names: 0 transitivity and 0 antisymmetry violations (evidence/F03116-natural-comparer-fuzz.cs.txt), so no inconsistent-comparer risk for List.Sort was found. Test: WindowsNaturalComparerOrdersNaturally.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.public WindowsRecycleBin(ILog? log = null) : this(log, WindowsRecycleBinSettingsSource.Instance)
Rationale: Public ctor binds the real registry settings source (WindowsRecycleBinSettingsSource.Instance); nothing else.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.internal WindowsRecycleBin(ILog? log, IRecycleBinSettingsSource settings, Action<string>? shellRecycle = null, Func<string, long, DateTime, bool>? shellRestore = null)
Rationale: Null settings rejected, seams default to the real VB FileSystem.DeleteFile (SendToRecycleBin, OnlyErrorDialogs) and RestoreViaShell; the seams are what keep tests off the real Recycle Bin (AGENTS.md rule). Tests construct it with fakes (RecycleBinCapacityGuardTests, WindowsRecycleBinRestoreGuardTests).

Lambda is the single place that touches the real bin for delete: FileSystem.DeleteFile with UIOption.OnlyErrorDialogs plus RecycleOption.SendToRecycleBin; only reached after eligibility and capacity checks in SendToRecycleBin. Never executed by this review (read only).

Ordering is right (arg check, drive-type eligibility, capacity guard with size-independent switches, shell call, then File.Exists check so a cancelled/aborted shell operation is never reported as success). Gap: eligibility uses the lexical drive root while the capacity guard resolves the real volume, so a path reached through a junction/symlink or a mounted folder to a removable or network volume is judged fixed-drive eligible and can still pass the guard with no BitBucket key; the shell may then delete permanently while the journal records a recycle. Proven: GetVolumePathNameW(junction\file)=D:\ vs GetPathRoot=C:\ on this machine; shell outcome not run (no Recycle Bin use). See P-RB-01. Tests: SendToRecycleBin_BinDisabled_ThrowsAndNeverCallsShell, SendToRecycleBin_BinOn_CallsShellOnce, RecycleEligibilityTests.
Thin forward of CanRecycle to RecycleEligibility with a blank-path guard; root-cause note (lexical root) lives in F03132 / P-RB-01. Test: WindowsRecycleBinRejectsInvalidArguments.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.public bool FitsInRecycleBin(string path, long fileSize)
Rationale: Capacity-only check with the caller's stat size; logs file name and size with InvariantCulture; returns false for every non-Fits verdict (refuse before journaling per F-WIN-2, ADR 0007 amendment). Reads registry/volume metadata only. Tests: FitsInRecycleBin_TooLarge_False, Evaluate_AtSafetyMargin_Boundary.

Refuses when CanRecycle is true, so it can never bypass the bin on a drive that has one, and re-checks File.Exists after File.Delete. CanRecycle is also false for 'unknown drive type', which makes the permanent route reachable there, but FileActionService.cs:588-592 only takes it after the AllowPermanentDelete opt-in and confirmation (Q-R8), so it is an accepted trade-off. Read-only files raise UnauthorizedAccessException to the caller, not swallowed. No unit test of File.Delete itself (would touch disk outside a temp dir).

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.public bool TryRestore(string originalPath, long expectedSize, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: Argument guard, then File.Exists(originalPath) refuses before any shell call so the Restore verb can never raise its modal replace/rename prompt (RV-P02); delegates to the seam. Caller UndoService.cs:326-330 also treats 'restore reported false but the file is back with the same size/mtime' as success. Tests: TryRestore_FileExistsAtOriginalPath_ReturnsFalseWithoutShellCall, TryRestore_PathFree_DelegatesToShellRestore.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.private bool RestoreViaShell(string originalPath, long expectedSize, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: Selection safety is strong: exactly one candidate must match folder+name+size+timestamp or nothing is restored; per-item COM failures are skipped and every non-selected item RCW is released immediately, selected item/verbs/Verbs()/Items()/recycle/shell released in finally; verb invocation goes through RestoreVerb (canonical undelete fallback). Defect (P3 hygiene): the foreach over the COM IEnumerable creates an IEnumVARIANT RCW that is never FinalReleased (not IDisposable), left to the GC finalizer. WaitForRestore timeout (1.8 s) is covered by UndoService's post-check. STA-hosting suspicion tested and dropped (evidence/F03125-sta-hosting-probe.cs.txt: MTA caller is not served by the main STA). Not executed against the real bin by this review. Tests: WindowsRecycleBinTryRestoreReturnsFalseWhenNothingMatches, candidate/verb tests; real restore only in Native NativeRecycleBinTests.

Index route: DoIt on the verb RCW chosen by RestoreVerb.FindIndex; the verb RCWs are collected in verbItems and released in the enclosing finally, so no leak if DoIt throws (exception propagates to the outer catch, logged, returns false). Test: FailingVerbPropagatesWithoutSecondAttempt.

Canonical route: InvokeVerb(\"undelete\") on the selected item, only used when no localized name matched (language independent); invoked at most once per restore (RestoreVerb.Invoke contract). Test: UnrecognisedLanguageUsesCanonicalVerb.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.private static bool WaitForRestore(string path, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: Polls IsExpectedFile 30 x 60 ms (about 1.8 s) plus a final check; blocking Thread.Sleep is acceptable because the method runs off the UI thread (UndoService Task.Run). A slow restore that finishes after the window returns false although it succeeded, which UndoService.cs:326-330 and RecoveryRetryService absorb with a same-size/mtime re-check.

Function: WindowsRecycleBin.private static bool IsExpectedFile(string path, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: File.Exists AND LastWriteTimeUtc exact equality (shell Restore is a same-volume move that preserves the timestamp); IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException mean 'not yet', other exceptions would propagate to RestoreViaShell's catch-all. Exact equality assumes the caller's expected value kept 100 ns ticks (it comes from the file stat taken before the recycle).
Same null-safe FinalReleaseComObject-if-COM pattern as ExplorerOrderService.Release; used on RCWs created inside this call only, so it cannot invalidate a reference held elsewhere.

Whitelist COMException, InvalidCastException, FormatException and RuntimeBinderException (late-bound missing property): per-item inspection failures skip the item, anything else (e.g. InvalidOperationException) aborts the whole restore and returns false, which is the safe direction. Test: PerItemFailure_IncludesRuntimeBinderButNotUnrelatedErrors.

Function: RecycleEligibility.internal static bool CanRecycle(string path, Func<string, DriveType?> driveTypeOf)
Rationale: Root cause of P-RB-01: Path.GetFullPath then Path.GetPathRoot then DriveInfo(root).DriveType == Fixed looks only at the textual root, so C:\junction-to-USB\x.jpg or C:\mnt\usbvolume\x.jpg counts as the fixed C: drive. UNC, \\?\UNC and device paths are correctly refused, \\?\C:\ is unwrapped, GetFullPath failures return false. Remedy: classify the volume that GetVolumePathName resolves (mount point) and also require that drive type. Tests (RecycleEligibilityTests) cover fixed/non-fixed/unknown/UNC/extended-local but no reparse point or mounted-folder case.

new DriveInfo(root).DriveType with ArgumentException/IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException mapped to null (unknown), which CanRecycle treats as not recyclable (fail closed for recycle). External USB hard disks report Fixed and do have a bin, so they stay eligible. Test: CanRecycle_UnknownDrive_ReturnsFalse (via the seam).

Removes the CJK '(&E)' accelerator by turning '(&' into '(' and then dropping every '&', and trims; null/whitespace returns empty. Only used for matching, never shown. Test: KnownRestoreLabelsInManyLanguagesAreRecognized.

Substring OrdinalIgnoreCase match against the localized-Restore fragments; a miss is harmless because Invoke falls back to the canonical undelete verb, so a language missing from the list (e.g. Norwegian gjenopprett) still restores. Test: OtherRecycleBinVerbsAreNeverTakenForRestore.
Returns the first matching index or -1; an empty list returns -1 (canonical route). Tests: FindIndexReturnsTheFirstRestoreVerb, EmptyVerbListUsesCanonicalVerb.

Function: RestoreVerb.internal static string Invoke(IReadOnlyList<string> verbNames, Action<int> invokeByIndex, Action<string> invokeCanonical)
Rationale: Exactly one route is invoked and its label returned (verb:N or undelete); an exception from either route propagates and no second attempt is made, so a failing DoIt cannot trigger a double restore. Tests: RecognisedNameInvokesOnlyThatVerb, FailingVerbPropagatesWithoutSecondAttempt.

Function: RecycleCandidateSelector.private static bool TimestampMatches(DateTime shellValueUtc, DateTime expectedUtc)
Rationale: |difference| < 1 s covers shell whole-second truncation or rounding of System.DateModified versus NTFS 100 ns ticks; because folder, name and size are also required and exactly one candidate may match, a one-second window cannot restore a different file silently. Tests: SelectorToleratesShellWholeSecondTimestamps, SelectorAcceptsAlternateTimestampReading.

Function: RecycleCandidateSelector.internal static bool IsMatch(RecycleCandidate candidate, string originalPath, long expectedSize, DateTime expectedLastWriteUtc)
Rationale: AND of folder, name, size and either timestamp reading (UTC digits or local-converted); null DeletedFrom or empty folder never matches. Tests: SelectorRequiresOriginalPathSizeAndTimestamp, SelectorDoesNotAcceptAmbiguousCandidateByMetadata.

Function: RecycleCandidateSelector.private static bool FolderMatches(string? deletedFrom, string? originalFolder)
Rationale: Null/empty on either side never matches; trailing separators trimmed, OrdinalIgnoreCase (NTFS semantic). Drive root folders keep their separator-less form on both sides consistently. Test: SelectorRequiresFolderPlusName.

Function: RecycleCandidateSelector.private static bool NameMatches(string? displayName, string fileName)
Rationale: Accepts the display name equal to the file name or to the name without its last extension (Explorer hides known extensions); multi-dot names handled by GetFileNameWithoutExtension; collisions between 'photo' and 'photo.jpg' fall to the exactly-one-candidate rule. Tests: SelectorMatchesDisplayNameWithoutExtension, SelectorMatchesMultiDotNameWithoutLastExtension.
